title: Strawberry Eton Mess
summary: Crisp homemade meringue, soft whipped cream and fresh and cooked strawberries, folded together just before serving.
equipment: piping bag with 1 cm plain nozzle or a spoon

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Meringue
steps.text: heat the oven to 100 °C (80 °C fan) and line the tray. Mix the sugar and cornflour. Whisk the whites, vanilla and salt until frothy, then add the sugar mix slowly and whisk to stiff, glossy peaks. Pipe or spread in thin zigzag strips. Cornflour helps the meringue stay crisp.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: bake 1 h 30 min until dry outside, then switch the oven off and leave 1 h to crisp. Cool. Drying in the oven makes the meringue crisp all the way through.

steps.title: Berries
steps.text: quarter 350 g of the strawberries and toss with 15 g of the sugar and the lemon juice. Mash the rest with the remaining sugar in the pan and boil 5 min to a thick sauce; cool. The cooked sauce adds deep colour and flavour.

steps.title: Cream
steps.text: whip the cream and icing sugar to soft peaks.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: break the meringue into bite-size pieces. Just before serving, fold the meringue, half the sauce and most of the berries roughly through the cream, pile into the bowls and spoon over the rest of the sauce and berries. Folding at the last moment keeps the meringue crunchy.

tips: A common mistake is mixing too early; the meringue goes soft in minutes.
Make the meringue up to a week ahead and keep it airtight.
Do not overwhip the cream; soft peaks fold best.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Keep the meringue airtight for 1 week, and the berries and sauce in the fridge for up to 2 days.
